I had a stroke 3 years ago. Temporarily lost function of right side (arm and leg) - it didn't affect my thought processes and I was back on my feet and fully functional in 4 months.

Yes and no. Brain damage is permanent as neurons generally do not regenerate like other forms of tissue. However, the brain has this wonderful trait called 'Neuroplasticity' which allows it to reallocate neural functions that were disabled due to neural damage to other, intact sections of the complex (to a limited extend, at any rate).

I remember the case of one German boy who was suffering from extreme epilepsy to the point that doctors had no other choice than to remove one hemisphere (i.e., half of) his brain.
